input.description:
Constrain two parts by a geometric rule between a reference on each: the rule is kept as a
joint of the kind it needs (a mate is planar), made where the parts are, so b moves no further
than the rule needs and keeps every motion it leaves free. Several constraints between one pair
add up. One undo step.

a.description:
Side a's reference: a joint origin, as joint.create takes it (a face for a plane, a circle
for an axis, a point).

angle.description: An angle constraint's angle, in degrees or an expression (needed for angle).

b.description: Side b's reference, as `a`; b is the part that moves.

flip.description:
Turn b over: its reference along a's instead of the way the rule puts it. Default: a mate
is against, a flush along, the others as the parts face now.

name.description: The constraint's name. Default: the rule and the first free number (Mate1).

offset.description:
The gap from a's reference to b's, in mm or an expression (a mate's or flush's gap, a
distance; needed for distance). Default: 0.

quiet.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

input.description:
Add a row to the configuration table, change one, rename it or delete it. A new row starts
from `from`'s cells, or the design's current values; `values` then sets cells. Rows are checked
against the table's rules, and a parameter value against the parameters it drives, before
anything changes. The design keeps its active row's values until a row is activated. One undo
step.

delete.description:
Delete the row instead; `from`, `values` and `rename` are then not used. The last row can't
be deleted while the table has rules. Default: false.

from.description:
A row to copy the cells of, by name or id. Default: the row's own cells, or the design's
current values for a new row.

name.description:
The row, by name (1 to 128 bytes once spaces at either end are dropped) or by id. A name the
table doesn't have adds a row (at most 2000); an id must be one of its rows.

rename.description:
A new name for the row, which must exist: 1 to 128 bytes once spaces at either end are
dropped, not another row's.

values.description: Cells to set, by column key as `config.table` lists it (`param:W`, `suppress:Block`, `material:Body1`…), or by a parameter's or a suppressed feature's name. A cell is an expression for a parameter, true or false (suppressed) for a feature, a material's name for a material column, and a look's name or a look object for a look column; at most 4096 bytes. Each key must be a column the table has.

Add, replace, delete or move the configuration table's rules, which drive parameters and
suppressions from conditions, in the order they run. Give `rule`, `rules`, or `id` with
`delete` or `index`. Every row is then checked against the rules; if one fails, nothing
changes. One undo step.

delete.description: With `id`: delete the rule. Default: false (move it to `index`).

id.description: Without `rule` or `rules`: the rule to delete or move, by id.

index.description:

rule.description: A rule to add, or to replace the rule with its id.

condition.description: When the rule applies, by `type`: `always`; `all` or `any` of `conditions` (1 to 64); `not` (`condition`); `parameter`, a parameter compared (`operator`) with an `expression`; or `suppression`, whether a feature (`feature`, by id) is suppressed (`value`). At most 64 conditions, 8 deep.

expression.description: An expression the parameter is compared with.

effect.description: What the rule does when its condition holds, by `type`: `drive_parameter` sets a parameter to an `expression`; `drive_suppression` suppresses a feature (`value` true) or not; `parameter_range` keeps a parameter from `minimum` to `maximum`; `allow_parameter_values` allows only the values of `expressions` (1 to 128).

length_unit.description: The unit of plain numbers in the rule's length expressions. Default: the replaced rule's, or the design's unit.

name.description: A name to show: 1 to 128 characters, not only spaces.

rules.description:

names.description:

millimetres as it is read (refused for a 3MF or glTF file, which states its own; ignored

up.description:
For a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino or glTF file only (refused for any other): which way is up
in the file. Default: z for STEP, IGES, FreeCAD and Rhino, y for glTF.

the previous flat-shading behavior; positive angles regenerate angle-weighted normals
across manifold edges below this angle. Omitted or null keeps authored OBJ normals and
smoothing groups, or flat shading when absent. Geometry stays unchanged.

origin.description:
Whether, once the mesh is read, scaled and stood up, the import's occurrence is moved so
the box around its bodies is centred on X and Y of the active component with its lowest
point on Z = 0 (the reply gives the shift as `moved_to_origin`). Default: false, so the
mesh keeps the coordinates its file gives it.

path.description:

meshes join the design as mesh bodies in a new component, placed in the active component.

states its own, and is refused `units`. The design keeps the millimetre mesh and not the
unit, so insert the file again to try another.

turns the import's component a quarter turn about X, so Y becomes Z, and the reply gives
its occurrence as `stand_up`; `z` keeps the file's axes. Any case.

the feature's name, the new bodies' names and the bodies taking part. A feature command's
parameters include it with

```ignore

```

Two keys `add_feature` also reads aren't here. `targets` it reads only for primitives; the
other commands that read it are the ones that combine bodies. `operation` it reads for every
feature (a cut where the active component has no bodies takes part in all of them), but only
the commands that combine bodies take one; those declare it with their own type

(parallel, perpendicular, angle, point_on_plane, point_on_line, line_on_plane) ties only some
directions or points and is made where the parts are. An expression given for `offset`,

a.description:
Side a: a joint origin, as an object in world coordinates or a joint origin's name. The
two sides must be on different occurrences.

angle.description:
The turn about that distance, in degrees or an expression; for an angle relation, its tilt
from mated. Default: none, or a half turn where that turns b less, so faces that already
meet stay as they are.

b.description: Side b: a joint origin, as `a`.

flip.description:

b's z against a's as two faces meet); true keeps two origins given at one point with the
same z and x as they are. A point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both,
or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is.

limits.description:
The limits of each value: [min, max] pairs, with null for a value without limits. Default:
none.

name.description:
The joint's name. Default: its type, `Joint` and the first number no joint's name has.

offset.description: The distance from a's frame to b's along z, in mm or an expression. Default: 0.

quiet.description: Leave out `dof` and `fixed` in the reply. Default: false.

value.description:

input.description:
Drive one value of a joint from `from` toward `to` on a copy of the design, and stop at the
first contact between the parts checked (bisected to `refine`), where a closed loop can't
close, or at a limit. Closed loops follow; contact sets don't stop it. The design is not
changed unless `apply` is true.

against.description: The parts that stay: each of `occurrences` is checked only against these.

apply.description:
Leave the design where the sweep stopped, in one undo step. Default: false: the design
is not changed.

budget_s.description:
Seconds the sweep may take (above 0, at most 86400): past them it stops and returns what
it found, `stopped_by` `budget`, and its work is then not capped. Default: no time budget;
the work caps (4096 samples, 64 bisection steps, 500 million triangle tests) stop it the
same way.

contact_sets.description: Check the pairs of the design's contact sets instead (not with `occurrences`).

exclude_pairs.description:
Pairs left out, such as a pin in its hole: `[a, b]`, each an occurrence's id or name; a
pair of bodies is left out when one is under `a` and the other under `b`. Default: none.

from.description: Where the sweep starts.

index.description: Which value (0 for a revolute's angle). Default: 0.

occurrences.description: The parts checked against each other. Default: every occurrence.

refine.description:
mm: the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last
clear value and the touching one (above 0, at most 1000). Default: 0.01.

report_gaps.description:
Report the nearest gap at every sample, and the nearest each part came to another

input.description:
Add a user parameter: a named number with a unit, or a named text. Features, sketches and
other parameters can use it by name. One undo step.

comment.description: A note to show with it.

expression.description: The value: a number, or an expression as text (`25 mm`, `W / 2`). For a text parameter, its text; quotes round it are optional.

favorite.description: List it with the favourites, first. Default: false.

name.description:
The new parameter's name: a letter or `_`, then letters, digits or `_`; not a unit's,
function's or constant's name, nor another parameter's.

unit.description:
The unit: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, `deg`, `rad`, `""` (no unit) or `text` (a text
parameter, whose expression is its text). Default: the expression's own unit, a length
in the design's units.

value.description: Another name for `expression`, read when `expression` isn't a number or text.

input.title: ParamAddParams

label: Add User Parameter

anyOf.description: A text parameter.

unit.description: Always `text`.

value.description: Always `null`: a text has no number.

anyOf.description: A number.

display_value.description: Its value in its own unit; `null` if it can't be worked out.

unit.description: Its unit; `""` for none.

value.description:
Its value in mm for a length and degrees for an angle, as in every reply; `null` if
it can't be worked out.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

params: name, expression, unit?: as parameters.change (text: a text parameter, its expression the text), comment?, favorite?: bool

input.description: What `parameters.change` takes, in the form it's read in: see [`ParamChangeParams`].

changes.description:
Several existing parameters at once, `{name: expression}`: they are checked together and
the design is rebuilt once, all or nothing. Renaming isn't done this way. When given,
no other key is read.

comment.description: A note to show with the parameter.

delete.description:
Delete this user parameter (refused while something uses it). When given as text, no
other key but `changes` is read.

expression.description:
The new value: a number, or an expression as text (`25 mm`, `W / 2`). A text
parameter's expression is its text, quotes round it optional. `name = value` renames
the parameter to `name` and sets the value (or sets `name` when the value is just
`name`). Needed unless `new_name`, `favorite` or `comment` is given.

favorite.description: List it with the favourites, first, or not.

name.description:
The parameter to change, by name: a user parameter, a sketch dimension or a feature's
named input. Spaces at either end are dropped.

new_name.description:
Rename the parameter: the expressions, feature inputs and dimensions that use it follow.
With an `expression` the new value is set too.

unit.description:
The unit: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, `deg`, `rad`, `""` (no unit) or `text`. Default:
the parameter's own, or for a new one its value's unit, a length in the design's units.

value.description: Another name for `expression`, read when `expression` isn't a number or text.

input.title: ParamChangeParams

label: Change Parameters

FailedFeature.description: A feature that failed to rebuild: its name and error.

changed_through.description:
Set when `name = expression` set the parameter that the changed value's expression named:
the name asked for.

display_value.description: Its value in its own unit; `null` if it can't be worked out.

errors.description: The features that failed to rebuild.

expression.description: The expression it has now; `null` when only its name, comment or favourite changed.

renamed.description: Set when the parameter was renamed (`new_name`, or `name = expression`).

restored.description: How many features reused an earlier result for the same inputs (a value set back).

switched.description: The features the configuration rules switched, when they did.

value.description:
Its value in mm for a length and degrees for an angle, as in every reply; `null` if it
can't be worked out.

from.description: The old name.

references_updated.description: How many expressions, feature inputs and dimensions were changed to use the new name.

to.description: The new name.

SwitchedFeature.description: A feature a configuration rule switched on or off.

name.description: Its name; `null` if it is gone.

anyOf.description: A parameter was deleted (`delete`).
Several parameters were set (`changes`).

changed.description:
Each changed parameter's value, in mm for a length and degrees for an angle; `null`
where it can't be worked out.

errors.description: The features that failed to rebuild.

restored.description: How many features reused an earlier result for the same inputs (a value set back).

switched.description: The features the configuration rules switched, when they did.

anyOf.description: One parameter was changed.

output.description: What `parameters.change` returns: one of three shapes, by what was asked.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

output.title: ParamChanged

params: name, expression (number or text), unit?: mm|cm|m|in|ft|deg|rad|""|text (new parameters default to their value's unit, a length the design's units; a text parameter's expression is its text, quotes round it optional: sketch texts' words are built from it), comment?, favorite?: bool, new_name?: rename (references follow; an expression `new = value` renames to `new` and sets value, or sets `new` when the expression is just `new`); or delete: name; or changes: {name: expression, …} (existing parameters, checked together and rebuilt once, all or nothing) → changed?: {name: value} (with changes), recomputed: features rebuilt, restored: features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused (e.g. a value set back), switched?: [{feature, name, suppressed}] (the configuration rules that switch a feature's suppression and read a parameter whose value changed run in their order, as on activation; driven parameters and restrictions wait for a configuration edit or activation)

input.description: Set a parameter's comment, a note shown with it. One undo step.

comment.description: The comment; empty text clears it.

label: Comment Parameter

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

params: name, comment

input.description:
Suggest completions for the word at the end of some expression text: parameters (by name,
anywhere in it), functions, constants and units. Changes nothing.

prefix.description:
The text before the cursor; the word being typed is its trailing letters, digits and
underscores. Default: empty, which lists every parameter, function and constant.

input.title: ExprCompleteParams

label: Complete Expression

detail.description: A parameter's expression and value, a function's signature, or a unit's kind.

text.description: The text to insert: a parameter's name, a function's name and `(`, a constant or a unit.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

suggestions.description:
Parameters first (names that start with the word, then the rest; favourites and user
parameters first, at most 200), then functions, the constant `pi` and units.

word.description: The word being completed; empty when the text ends in something else.

params: prefix?: the text before the cursor → word, suggestions [{text, kind: parameter|function|unit|constant, detail}]

input.description:
Bind a body of a render setup to optical numbers (glass, tinted media, subsurface
scattering), for the CPU or GPU renderer, in one undo step. The design's geometry and engineering
materials don't change. The setup may render on the CPU or GPU.

body_index.description: The body's place in the render scene, from 0, as `render.library.targets` gives it.

body_name.description: The body's name at that place; a body that moved in the list is refused.

expected_revision.description:
The design's revision when the caller last read it, as `document.inspect` gives it. If
the design changed since, the call is refused: read it again and retry.

name.description: The render setup, saved or new.

optics.description: The body's optical numbers, for the CPU or GPU renderer. Each field has a default: `{}` is clear glass with a refractive index of 1.5. These are render-only numbers, not an engineering material.

absorption_per_mm.description: How much light the inside absorbs per mm, as linear red, green and blue: each 0 or more. Default: none.

boundary.description: How the body's surface bounds the medium: `thin_sheet` (a sheet of `thickness_mm`), `closed_box` or `closed_mesh` (the thickness comes from the geometry). Default: closed_mesh.

model.description: Advanced Glass interface. Default: null (no model). A model requires the interface IOR to stay in [1, 3], including the full 380 to 780 nm range when dispersion is enabled.

dispersion.description: Three-band chromatic dispersion. Default: null (no dispersion).

roughness.description: Isotropic roughness, from 0 (smooth) to 1. Very small positive values can exceed transport precision. Default: 0.

thin_film.description: One lossless film. Default: null (no film).

thickness_nm.description: Film thickness in nm, from 0 to 100000. Zero has no film effect.

shadow_transmission.description: Let light through for shadows too. Default: false.

anisotropy.description: Which way it scatters: -0.95 (back) to 0.95 (forward). Default: 0, every way alike.

scattering_per_mm.description: How often light scatters per mm: 0 to 100.

subsurface.description: Light scattering inside the body, as in wax or skin; `null` for none. Default: none.

thickness_mm.description: A thin sheet's thickness (mm); 0 for a closed boundary. Default: 0.

replace.description: Replace optics the body already has. Without it, such a body is refused.

set.description: Changes to the setup made with the binding, as `render.settings.set` takes them: at most 13 of the setup's fields. Default: none.

input.title: OpticsBindParams

label: Save Optical Binding

certification.description:
What the image producer checks before it draws the body: closed topology and nested
containment.

geometry_and_engineering_unchanged.description: Always true: the design's geometry and engineering data don't change.

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

setup.description: The setup as saved, as the render settings commands give it.

params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: complete numerical setup patch; body_index and body_name: exact captured target; expected_revision; optics:{ior,absorption_per_mm:[r,g,b],boundary:closed_mesh|closed_box|thin_sheet,thickness_mm,shadow_transmission,subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm,anisotropy},model?:{roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}}; replace?:false. The optional model adds isotropic rough transmission, three-band dispersion and one lossless coherent film. CPU models require explicit Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. Stores stable definition/feature/occurrence identity in one undo without modifying engineering geometry/materials. CPU Path consumes at most 128 certified optical targets; the legacy non-Path producer retains eight. Without options.path, sheets and axis-aligned boxes retain the existing transport. Explicit progressive options.path enables exact closed-mesh certification, bounded nested convex-parent media, Beer/Snell/Fresnel and thin transmitted shadows; touching or unproven boundaries and closed transmitted-shadow connections refuse explicitly. Existing subsurface parameters may be consumed on certified closed Path media with denoising explicitly off; scalar free-flight/HG walks and separate Beer absorption are supported without refracting-boundary next-event approximation. A zero scattering rate preserves transport. GPU nested media require separate job.options.nested_media and producer certification. Unresolved or incompatible targets refuse atomically.

input.description: Remove one body's optical binding from a saved render setup, in one undo step.

expected_revision.description:
The design's revision when the caller last read it, as `document.inspect` gives it. If
the design changed since, the call is refused: read it again and retry.

target.description: A body, by the identity a render setup keeps for it, as the setup's `surfaces` or `optics` list gives it. A component and its occurrence path are both 0 and empty for a body outside components.

component.description: The id of the component the body is in, or 0 outside components.

definition.description: The design or component definition that holds the body: 1 to 1024 bytes, without control characters.

feature.description: The id of the feature that made the body: 1 or more.

occurrence_path.description: The occurrence ids from the top of the design down to the body's occurrence, each 1 or more and none twice; empty outside components.

label: Remove Optical Binding

param_warnings.description: In the warn parameter-check mode: what the call's parameters got wrong.

removed.description: Whether the body had optics to remove; `false` leaves the setup as it was.

params: name: saved setup; target: exact saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path; expected_revision. Removes only that optical assignment in one undo without a device or file access.

label: Set Render Output Size
params: width, height: 1..16384; custom?: bool. Validated Render output draft request; headless echo only, no design edits or job. The UI separately limits new selections to 8192 per side, 33554432 output pixels and the selected rendering profile.

input.description: An image request. With `progressive: true` it is the GPU form, without it the runtime form; each refuses the other form's keys. Render Image captures the product and queues a job; Check Render Request checks the request and estimates its cost without queuing anything. Neither changes the design.

adaptive.description: GPU: adaptive sampling: `pilot_samples`, `min_samples`, `relative_error`, `absolute_error` and `coverage_error`. Default: none, the same samples for every pixel.

aging.description: Aging layers for the bodies, at most 8: with `integrator: raytrace` on the CPU, or on the GPU with `progressive: true`; the raster executor refuses them. Default: none.

backdrop.description: GPU: a gradient behind the product, as Regrade Linear Master's `presentation` takes it. Default: none.

caustics.description: GPU: photon caustics: `photons`, `radius_mm`, `max_depth`, `seed` and the optional `area_lights`, `environment`, `guided_emission` and `refresh_per_pass`. Default: none.

clamp_indirect.description: GPU: cap each contribution from the first bounce on at this value, from 0.000001 to 1000000, keeping its hue. Biased. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`. Default: none.

denoise.description: GPU: denoise the image. Without `progressive: true`, only `false`. Default: false.

denoise_diagnostics.description: GPU: keep the denoiser's guide mask, for `render.export` with `format: denoise_mask`. Default: false.

denoise_settings.description: GPU: the denoiser's `passes` (1 to 3), `strength` (0 to 1), `firefly_suppression` and `optical_filter`.

environment.description: Without `progressive`: a CPU HDR environment, with `integrator: raytrace`: `{path, expected_sha256?, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for a file or `{resource, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for an HDR saved in the design. With `progressive: true`: a GPU environment, by `kind`: `{kind: builtin_hdr, id, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`, `{kind: hdr, path, expected_sha256?, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}`, `{kind: embedded_hdr, resource, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}` or `{kind: sky, gradient?, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`. An HDR's `resource` and `expected_sha256` are its SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex digits. Default: none.

finishing.description: GPU: creative finishing, as Regrade Linear Master's `presentation` takes it: `looks`, `photographic`, `bloom`, `rgb_gain`, `contrast`, `saturation` and `vignette`. Default: none.

integrator.description: `raster` or `raytrace` (CPU ray tracing, in a build with it). With `progressive: true`, only `raster`. Default: raster.

led_samples.description: CPU only: the samples for the whole LED strip: 1, 4, 16 or 64. Needs `led_strip`. Default: 16.

led_strip.description: CPU only, with `integrator: raytrace`: a continuous LED strip, a rectangle in world mm (`center_mm`, `length_mm`, `width_mm`, `length_axis`, `width_axis`, `color`, `intensity`), lit as area lights.

lens.description: GPU: a thin lens, `{aperture_radius_mm, focus_distance_mm}`. Default: none, a pinhole camera.

lighting.description: GPU: studio lighting in place of the implicit studio. Default: none.

linear_exr.description: GPU: keep the raw linear FLOAT32 master, for `render.export` with `format: exr`. Default: false.

max_depth.description: GPU: the most bounces, from 1 to 64. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

metal_energy_compensation.description: GPU: restore the energy rough isotropic metals lose. Default: false.

nested_media.description: GPU: trace strictly nested solids (glass in glass, an air bubble) as nested media. Default: false.

progressive.description: `true`: the GPU form, rendered progressively by the GPU path tracer; the keys marked GPU apply. `false` or left out: the runtime form, for the raster executor or, with `integrator: raytrace`, the CPU ray tracer. Default: false.

raytrace.description: Without `progressive`: the CPU ray tracer's options (lights, reflections, `path`, `progressive` sampling, `output`, `budget` and others; see docs/render-jobs.md), with `integrator: raytrace`. With `progressive: true`: the GPU's `dielectrics`, `clear_coats` and `textures` overrides, each a list.

replace.description: Render Image: cancel the design's active and waiting render jobs before this one starts. Check Render Request ignores it. Default: false.

samples.description: GPU: samples per pixel, from 1 to 65536. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

seed.description: GPU: the random seed. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

settings.description: A whole render setup, as `render.settings.get` gives one, used without saving it; a setup with a `job` as for `setup`. Not with `setup`. Without either: the default setup, seen from the current camera or fitted to the product.

setup.description: A saved render setup, by name. A setup with a saved `job` decides the method and its options, and only `replace` and `studio_weights` may come with it (`studio_weights` only where its method takes them). Not with `settings`.

studio_weights.description: Three visibility weights, each from 0 to 1, for the studio's sources: with the raster executor, or on the GPU with its implicit studio (no `lighting` and no environment). Never saved.

supersampling.description: GPU: 1 or 2. At 2 the image is traced at twice the width and height and averaged down. Default: 1.

texture_filtering.description: GPU: filter surface maps by the ray's footprint (mip levels and bounded anisotropy). Default: false, which samples the finest level bilinearly.

tone_map.description: GPU: the tone response, `reinhard` or `aces_fitted`. Default: reinhard.

transmission_samples.description: GPU: 1, 2 or 4 strata for the first Fresnel branch. Default: 1.

transparent_background.description: Leave the background transparent. Default: false.

volume.description: GPU: one homogeneous medium: `min_mm`, `max_mm`, `extinction_per_mm` (0 to 1000), `scattering_albedo` [r, g, b] and `anisotropy` (-0.95 to 0.95). Default: none.

params: setup?: saved name OR settings?: full RenderSetup. A typed job selects raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path and its numerical options plus embedded HDR before dispatch; only replace and transient studio_weights may accompany it. Without job, the legacy runtime controls below remain available. See docs/render-settings.md. studio_weights?: three finite 0..1 visibility weights for raster or implicit GPU studio sources only; never saved. integrator?: raster (default) or raytrace; progressive?: false (registered GPU path, CPU integrator/LED options are mutually exclusive); texture_filtering?: false (GPU); CPU raytrace.texture_filtering?: false. Explicitly enables ray-footprint mip and bounded anisotropic map filtering on GPU, and bounded anisotropic filtering on CPU. GPU filtering off retains bilinear LOD0; CPU filtering off retains isotropic mip selection, using the coarsest available mip when footprint data is unavailable. samples?: 1..65536; max_depth?: 1..64; seed?: u32 for progressive; raytrace?: bounded runtime progressive/primary_samples/lights/punctual_lights/area_lights/area_samples/seed/exposure_ev/shadows/reflections/anisotropic_faces/emissions/surface_effects/dielectrics/environment options, only with raytrace. CPU raytrace.lens?: {aperture_radius_mm:0..10000000,focus_distance_mm:0.000001..1000000000}; positive aperture requires explicit CPU progressive sampling and a bounded perspective camera; absent/zero keeps the original CPU ray stream. See docs/render-thin-lens.md. CPU raytrace.volume?: one HomogeneousVolume box with world-mm min_mm/max_mm, extinction_per_mm:0..1000, RGB scattering_albedo:0..1 and anisotropy:-0.95..0.95. Positive extinction requires explicit Indirect lighting and cannot combine with Glass/SSS or surface Denoise. Physical eye/pupil prefixes and the orthographic line/box union preserve camera/model framing under existing ray/profile caps. See docs/render-cpu-volume.md. CPU raytrace.sun? uses the shared finite-disk Sun contract; raytrace.sky? uses {gradient,rotation_rad,intensity}. Both require explicit Indirect lighting, and gradient Sky excludes a constant/HDR environment. Their medium NEE uses the HG response/PDF and physical light source; see docs/render-cpu-celestial.md. CPU transparent_background?:false exports straight-alpha primary geometry coverage for fixed/progressive sampling; body/face opacity must remain 1, and active bloom/backdrop/photographic effects require opaque output. CPU raytrace.output?: {tone_map,finishing,backdrop,linear_exr}; shared presentation supports up to 8192 per side and 33554432 output pixels, CPU exposure remains raytrace.exposure_ev; raw FLOAT32 EXR is retained only at final completion. CPU raytrace.budget?: compact (legacy default), studio or workstation; see docs/render-cpu-resource-profiles.md for explicit image/geometry/memory/work limits. CPU raytrace.progressive?: {samples_per_pixel:1..profile limit, seed:u32}; requires primary_samples:1 and selected reflections.samples:1; area/LED sources and certified planar anisotropy/thin-sheet/axis-aligned-box dielectric continuations share the existing bounded transport and compatibility checks. See docs/render-cpu-progressive.md; environment?: {path: scoped HDR, expected_sha256?: inspected digest, rotation_radians: 0, intensity: 1, samples: 16} OR {resource: saved HDR digest, rotation_radians, intensity, samples}; embedded resources cannot combine with path/hash; explicit sRGB/D65 HDR primaries required. Opaque CPU preview with selected mirror/rough-specular reflections and certified planar anisotropy. HDR with rough reflections or anisotropy requires fully metallic selected bodies and all effective faces; unsupported combinations refuse. Optional raytrace.path:{max_depth:1..64} enables CPU diffuse/specular GI with matched rectangle/HDR light and BSDF MIS plus certified closed-mesh Glass. It requires explicit progressive camera sampling, primary_samples:1 and traced shadows; selected reflections and certified anisotropy refuse before HDR IO without changing intent. CPU Path dielectric subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm:0..100,anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} enables homogeneous free-flight/HG walks inside certified closed media; positive rates require denoising off. Contained light connections include scattering survival; closed refractive light connections and combining Glass with external volume remain unsupported. Absent path keeps the old certified thin_sheet/closed_box producer and refuses subsurface intent explicitly. See docs/render-cpu-general-glass.md and render-raytrace-dielectrics.md. CPU emissions are visible radiance and may light neighbors through sampled Path continuation, without mesh-emitter next-event sampling; surface_effects change roughness/shading normals without geometry changes. led_strip?: continuous world-mm LED rectangle recipe; led_samples?: 1/4/16/64 for the whole strip, default16. At most8directional+8punctual+4rectangle/LED sources; shared area N. See docs/render-light-union.md. transparent_background?: false; replace?: false. With progressive:true, raytrace instead accepts GPU dielectrics/clear_coats/textures; environment instead accepts tagged hdr/embedded_hdr/sky with rotation_rad/intensity; file hdr supports expected_sha256, embedded_hdr uses a document resource digest. See docs/render-hdr-resources.md. GPU lens, studio lighting, tone_map, denoise, clamp_indirect?: 0.000001..1000000 (biased; caps each contribution from the first bounce on, keeping its hue; see docs/render-path.md), bounded finishing/backdrop and linear_exr retention are also available. CPU raytrace and GPU top-level controls accept supersampling:1|2 (default 1; doubles internal width and height at 2, averages scene-linear premultiplied samples before tone mapping, exports selected dimensions), denoise_settings:{passes:1..3,strength:0..1,firefly_suppression:bool,optical_filter:bool}, and denoise_diagnostics:false. Optical filtering defaults to true for eligible mirror/glass guides; optical_filter:false restores legacy opaque-only display denoising. Guides and diagnostics retain their independent eligibility policy and conservative highlight protection. CPU raytrace.threads:0..64 selects bounded automatic workers at 0 (default), serial work at 1 or an explicit count from 2 through 64. Resource checks include internal image buffers and worker scratch. See docs/render-quality-controls.md. Both path tracers accept optional metal_energy_compensation: true for rough isotropic metals (inside CPU raytrace or top-level GPU). Both methods accept optional caustics {photons:1..1048576,radius_mm:0.000001..1000000,max_depth:1..64,seed:u32,area_lights?:false,environment?:false,guided_emission?:false,refresh_per_pass?:false} (inside CPU raytrace; top-level GPU). Optical assignments accept optional model {roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}. CPU advanced models require Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. GPU adaptive?: {pilot_samples:16..256,min_samples:16..samples,relative_error:0..1,absolute_error:0.000001..1000000,coverage_error:0.001..0.25} allocates independent production budgets; pilots are discarded, not a certified error guarantee. transmission_samples?:1|2|4 stratifies the first Fresnel branch with extra path cost. volume?:{min_mm:[x,y,z],max_mm:[x,y,z],extinction_per_mm:0..1000,scattering_albedo:[r,g,b],anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} is one finite homogeneous world-mm medium; active media require explicit lighting/environment and refuse glass, denoise and multiple transmission strata. These fields also persist in GPU job.options. See docs/render-materials/TRANSPORT-MASTER-BATCH-2026-10-23.md; see docs/render-transmission.md, render-environment.md, render-runtime-textures.md, render-thin-lens.md, render-studio-lighting.md and render-denoise.md. Optional CPU raytracing requires a raytrace-cpu build and native host, checked before scene capture. Stale geometry is rejected. See docs/render-jobs.md

input.description: An image request. With `progressive: true` it is the GPU form, without it the runtime form; each refuses the other form's keys. Render Image captures the product and queues a job; Check Render Request checks the request and estimates its cost without queuing anything. Neither changes the design.

adaptive.description: GPU: adaptive sampling: `pilot_samples`, `min_samples`, `relative_error`, `absolute_error` and `coverage_error`. Default: none, the same samples for every pixel.

aging.description: Aging layers for the bodies, at most 8: with `integrator: raytrace` on the CPU, or on the GPU with `progressive: true`; the raster executor refuses them. Default: none.

backdrop.description: GPU: a gradient behind the product, as Regrade Linear Master's `presentation` takes it. Default: none.

caustics.description: GPU: photon caustics: `photons`, `radius_mm`, `max_depth`, `seed` and the optional `area_lights`, `environment`, `guided_emission` and `refresh_per_pass`. Default: none.

clamp_indirect.description: GPU: cap each contribution from the first bounce on at this value, from 0.000001 to 1000000, keeping its hue. Biased. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`. Default: none.

denoise.description: GPU: denoise the image. Without `progressive: true`, only `false`. Default: false.

denoise_diagnostics.description: GPU: keep the denoiser's guide mask, for `render.export` with `format: denoise_mask`. Default: false.

denoise_settings.description: GPU: the denoiser's `passes` (1 to 3), `strength` (0 to 1), `firefly_suppression` and `optical_filter`.

environment.description: Without `progressive`: a CPU HDR environment, with `integrator: raytrace`: `{path, expected_sha256?, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for a file or `{resource, rotation_radians?, intensity?, samples?}` for an HDR saved in the design. With `progressive: true`: a GPU environment, by `kind`: `{kind: builtin_hdr, id, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`, `{kind: hdr, path, expected_sha256?, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}`, `{kind: embedded_hdr, resource, rotation_rad?, intensity?, assume_linear_srgb?}` or `{kind: sky, gradient?, rotation_rad?, intensity?}`. An HDR's `resource` and `expected_sha256` are its SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex digits. Default: none.

finishing.description: GPU: creative finishing, as Regrade Linear Master's `presentation` takes it: `looks`, `photographic`, `bloom`, `rgb_gain`, `contrast`, `saturation` and `vignette`. Default: none.

integrator.description: `raster` or `raytrace` (CPU ray tracing, in a build with it). With `progressive: true`, only `raster`. Default: raster.

led_samples.description: CPU only: the samples for the whole LED strip: 1, 4, 16 or 64. Needs `led_strip`. Default: 16.

led_strip.description: CPU only, with `integrator: raytrace`: a continuous LED strip, a rectangle in world mm (`center_mm`, `length_mm`, `width_mm`, `length_axis`, `width_axis`, `color`, `intensity`), lit as area lights.

lens.description: GPU: a thin lens, `{aperture_radius_mm, focus_distance_mm}`. Default: none, a pinhole camera.

lighting.description: GPU: studio lighting in place of the implicit studio. Default: none.

linear_exr.description: GPU: keep the raw linear FLOAT32 master, for `render.export` with `format: exr`. Default: false.

max_depth.description: GPU: the most bounces, from 1 to 64. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

metal_energy_compensation.description: GPU: restore the energy rough isotropic metals lose. Default: false.

nested_media.description: GPU: trace strictly nested solids (glass in glass, an air bubble) as nested media. Default: false.

progressive.description: `true`: the GPU form, rendered progressively by the GPU path tracer; the keys marked GPU apply. `false` or left out: the runtime form, for the raster executor or, with `integrator: raytrace`, the CPU ray tracer. Default: false.

raytrace.description: Without `progressive`: the CPU ray tracer's options (lights, reflections, `path`, `progressive` sampling, `output`, `budget` and others; see docs/render-jobs.md), with `integrator: raytrace`. With `progressive: true`: the GPU's `dielectrics`, `clear_coats` and `textures` overrides, each a list.

replace.description: Render Image: cancel the design's active and waiting render jobs before this one starts. Check Render Request ignores it. Default: false.

samples.description: GPU: samples per pixel, from 1 to 65536. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

seed.description: GPU: the random seed. Without `progressive: true`, only `null`.

settings.description: A whole render setup, as `render.settings.get` gives one, used without saving it; a setup with a `job` as for `setup`. Not with `setup`. Without either: the default setup, seen from the current camera or fitted to the product.

setup.description: A saved render setup, by name. A setup with a saved `job` decides the method and its options, and only `replace` and `studio_weights` may come with it (`studio_weights` only where its method takes them). Not with `settings`.

studio_weights.description: Three visibility weights, each from 0 to 1, for the studio's sources: with the raster executor, or on the GPU with its implicit studio (no `lighting` and no environment). Never saved.

supersampling.description: GPU: 1 or 2. At 2 the image is traced at twice the width and height and averaged down. Default: 1.

texture_filtering.description: GPU: filter surface maps by the ray's footprint (mip levels and bounded anisotropy). Default: false, which samples the finest level bilinearly.

tone_map.description: GPU: the tone response, `reinhard` or `aces_fitted`. Default: reinhard.

transmission_samples.description: GPU: 1, 2 or 4 strata for the first Fresnel branch. Default: 1.

transparent_background.description: Leave the background transparent. Default: false.

volume.description: GPU: one homogeneous medium: `min_mm`, `max_mm`, `extinction_per_mm` (0 to 1000), `scattering_albedo` [r, g, b] and `anisotropy` (-0.95 to 0.95). Default: none.

chain of sketch lines, or edge flanges on a sheet's edges. Thickness, K-factor, bend radius

body.description: Edge: the sheet metal body. Default: the sheet with an edge nearest the first point.

body_names.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

corner_relief.description:

rule's. Refused on a base or contour flange.

curves.description: Contour: the open chain's lines (curve ids; arcs aren't supported yet), 1 to 1000.

distance.description: Contour: how far the flange runs from the sketch plane, positive.

edges.description: Edge: the edges that get a flange.

flip.description:

to the other side of the chain. Edge: the flanges bend the other way. Default: false.

height.description:

(an edge's own `height` replaces it). Required for an edge flange.

sharp (inner), or past 90° the line square to the flange touching the bend's outside

name.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

participants.description:

face; below 90° the bend's end on that face). Default: inside.

profiles.description: Base: which of the sketch's profiles become the sheet. Default: all of them.

radius.description: Edge: the inner bend radius. Default: the sheet's rule's.

reverse.description: Contour: the flange runs from the sketch plane the other way. Default: false.

rule.description:

then.description:
Edge: further bends, each a flange on the far edge of the one before (at most 16). Refused
on a base or contour flange.

type.description:
Which flange: base, edge or contour, in any case. Default: edge when `edges` is given,
else contour when `curves` is given, else base.

Flip.description: false keeps the plane's own side; true turns it about its y axis (about x when y does not point upward) so the sketch's y axis stays upward; "x" or "y" (any case) turns it about that axis of the plane.

Frame.description:
Which coordinates an explicit plane is in: `world` (the default) or the active component's
own, `component`.

InsidePlane.description: Not taken here, in any form: the call is refused, and the message says where it belongs. Put it inside `plane`.

LengthExpr.description: A length: a number in the design's length unit, or an expression such as "w / 2" or "30 mm".

Point3.description: A point in mm: [x, y, z] or {"x", "y", "z"}.

body.description: Goes with `index`: give both or neither.

index.description: Goes with `body`: give both or neither.

SketchPlane.description: A plane: XY, XZ or YZ (or Top, Front or Right; any case), a construction plane's name or feature id, a picked planar face {"face": [x, y, z], "body"?, "index"?, "path"?, "fixed"?}, or an explicit plane {"origin"?, "x_dir", "y_dir"}: two directions [x, y, z] that aren't parallel and an origin in mm, numbers only (default: the origin).

input.description: The keys of a `sketch.create` call.

activate_part.description:
Only on a face of a body of another component than the active one: activate that
component at the picked placement first, as `component.activate` would, and make the
sketch there. It stays active afterwards and the reply's `activated` names it. Default:
false.

face.description: Refused: it belongs inside `plane`.

flip.description:
Not on a face: sketch the plane from its other side, so the normal and the default
extrude direction are reversed. Default: false.

frame.description:
Which coordinates an explicit plane is in. Default: world. Only for an explicit plane
`{origin, x_dir, y_dir}`; the reply's `frame` says which, with a `note` when the active
component is moved or turned.

offset.description: Move the plane this far along its normal (mm or a length expression), before `flip`.

plane.description:
The plane to sketch on: XY, XZ or YZ (also Top, Front, Right), a construction plane's
name or id, a picked planar face `{face: [x, y, z], body?, index?, path?, fixed?}`, or an
explicit plane `{origin?, x_dir, y_dir}` in mm. Default: XY. On XY, the sketch's x and y
run along world +X and +Y; on XZ, +X and -Z; on YZ, +Y and +Z. A face of a sheet metal
body attaches to its panel instead, in the flat pattern's coordinates; `fixed: true` keeps
the plane where the face is now. A named plane is the active component's own.

project_edges.description:
Only on a picked face: project the face's edges into the sketch. Default: the session's
Auto Project setting.

input.description:
Dimension one or two sketch entities: a length, distance, radius, diameter, angle or ellipse
half-axis, driving the sketch (it adds a parameter) or only measuring (`driven: true`). The
kind follows from the entities, `type` and where `text_at` is. One undo step.

driven.description:
True to place a driven (reference) dimension: it measures, has no parameter and does not
constrain. Default: false.

entities.description: The entities to dimension, one or two.

half_axes.description:
For an ellipse with type auto: true gives the half-axis `text_at` picks, false the minor
radius wherever `text_at` is. Default: true.

if_redundant.description:
`driven` (any case): when the sketch already determines the dimension, place it as a
driven (reference) dimension instead of refusing it; the reply then has `redundant` and
`determined_by`. Any other text refuses it. Read only when the dimension turns out to be
determined, and not for a driven dimension.

orientation.description:
With type auto or distance: `horizontal` or `vertical` measures along that axis, as
type does. Any other text is ignored.

previous_axis.description:
For an ellipse with type auto: `major` or `minor`, the half-axis an earlier placement
chose, kept while `text_at` is near the boundary between them (any case; other text is
ignored).

scale_about_origin.description:
Scale about the sketch origin even when the drawing is free. Default: false. Not read
for a driven dimension.

scale_sketch.description:
When this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size
(no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), scale the whole sketch
to the value instead of distorting it (the reply's `scaled` is the factor). A free
drawing uses its own centre. A drawing tied to the origin scales about the origin.
Default: false. Not read for a driven dimension.

is), distance, horizontal (or distance_x), vertical (or distance_y), length, radius,
diameter, major or minor (an ellipse's half-axis), angle, sweep (an arc's angle),
arc_length (arclength), overall_length (a slot's overall length), offset. Other text is no
known type: the entities' default measure (a length or a radius), with no choice by
`text_at`.

value.description:
The dimension's value: a number (in the design's units, or degrees for an angle) or an
expression such as `"width / 2"` or `"50 mm"`; or `name = expression` (also `#name =
expression`), which adds the user parameter `name` and dimensions with it (refused when the
name is taken or reserved; the reply's `defined` names it). Default: what the geometry
measures now. Not read for a driven dimension, which has no value (a definition is refused
there).

params: entities: [refs] (a line midpoint is "mid:line_id"; a model edge or vertex, {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, is projected into the sketch first and measured there: a point against the projected edge measures the distance to it), type?: auto|distance|horizontal|distance_x|vertical|distance_y|length|radius|diameter|major|minor|angle, value?: number or expression (default: current; a bare number is in the design's units, e.g. 2 means 2 in in an inch design; give a unit such as "50 mm" to override), or `name = expression` (e.g. "width = 40"; also `#name = expression`), which adds the user parameter `name` with that expression and dimensions with `name` (refused when the name is taken or reserved; the reply's `defined` names it); text_at?: [x, y]. Two points or a line off the axes: with auto, text_at across from them (between the perpendiculars through them, or a tenth of their distance past) is the distance between them; pulled further past an end, up or down from it horizontal, sideways vertical. Two midpoints: placing text above or below their bounding box measures horizontally, beside it vertically, anywhere else (inside it or past its corners) the distance between them. Two lines: the angle between them (acute, or 180° − it when the value is nearer that) unless text_at picks a sector. A line and a circle or arc: the distance from the line to its edge (the gap, or how far the edge reaches past a line that cuts it; 0 is tangent); dimension the centre point for the distance to the centre. A point and a circle or arc: the distance from the point to its edge (or how far within it a point inside lies). Two circles or arcs: the gap between their edges (or how far they overlap when they cross, or the narrowest gap between them when one lies inside the other), or the centre-to-centre distance when they are the two caps of a slot. An ellipse: a half-axis, the distance from the centre to an axis end (major or minor; with auto, text_at pulled across the major axis gives the major half-axis, pulled out past an end of it the minor one, the minor without text_at; previous_axis?: major|minor, the half-axis an earlier placement chose, kept while text_at is near the boundary between them; the reply's axis names the one chosen; with auto, when a driving dimension already holds one half-axis (or its whole axis), the other one, wherever text_at is; without its major axis line the major half-axis goes to the ellipse's own major end, without its minor axis line the minor half-axis is the minor radius); any other type, radius among them, the minor radius; an ellipse's axis line with auto: its length, the whole axis, wherever text_at is; half_axes?: bool (default true; false: with auto, the minor radius wherever text_at is, as before half-axes, which the Dimension tool sends with Draw ellipses with their axes off). An arc and one of its end points: the arc's length (type arc_length does it from the arc alone). A dimension the sketch already determines is refused (naming what determines it); if_redundant?: "driven" places it as a driven (reference) dimension instead. scale_sketch?: bool (the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference, on by default): when this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size (no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), the whole sketch scales to the value instead of distorting: about the origin when the drawing is tied to it (joined to the origin, or constrained to a sketch axis), otherwise about the middle of the drawing, so it stays where it was drawn (#11043); scale_about_origin?: bool (default false; the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference) scales about the origin always, as before #11043. input.description:

`params` its parameters; `dimensions` gives the sizes to place, by role, as driving
dimensions. With `as_drawn` every other size of the shape is placed at its size as drawn
(a size the sketch already determines is left out); with `locate` the shape is then placed
from the sketch origin with horizontal and vertical distances, only where each takes freedom
away. Either one makes `dimensions` optional. A size the sketch already has is placed as a
driven (reference) dimension rather than refused.

and vertical distances from the origin to its points, centres first, each kept only where
it removes freedom, so a shape anchored to the origin or to placed geometry gets none. A
point on an axis goes onto that axis instead of getting a distance of 0. Default: false.

input.description:
Move bodies so that a point, face, plane or frame on them meets another one, as a feature in
the timeline (one undo step). Each side is one of: a point (`from`, `to`), a planar face
picked by a point on it (`from_face`, `to_face`), a plane (`from_plane`, `to_plane`) or a frame
(`from_frame`, `to_frame`); give one key for each side. A plane or a frame is worked out again
whenever the design changes, so the bodies follow it. Faces, planes and frames also turn the
bodies so that they meet (the first side's face against the second's, or with `flip` side by
side); a point onto a plane moves along the plane's normal. `axes` keeps the move to some
world axes and only goes with two points. Align makes no body, so `body_name` and `body_names`
do nothing here (as for Remove), and `participants` changes nothing in the result.

angle.description:
A turn about the target's direction (a face's normal, a plane's normal or a frame's z)
after the move, in degrees or an expression. Needs a face, a plane or a frame as the
target. Default: none.

axes.description:
Which world axes the offset moves along, with a point on each side: [x, y, z] booleans,
at least one true. Default: all three. Refused with a face, plane or frame.

bodies.description: The bodies to move, by name: one, or a list of 1 to 10 000.

body_names.description: Names for the new bodies, in order.

flip.description:
With faces, planes or frames: true turns the bodies so that the two normals point the same
way, instead of facing each other. Default: false.

from.description:
Where the move starts, on the bodies. Not read when `from_face` is a point; not with
`from_plane` or `from_frame` (the handler refuses both).

from_face.description:
A point on a planar face of the bodies to start from: the bodies turn so that the face
meets the target's. When it is a point, `from` is not read. Not with `from_plane` or
`from_frame`.

from_frame.description:
A frame to start from, in place of the point, face or plane; the bodies turn so that it
meets the target. Not with `from`, `from_face` or `from_plane`.

from_plane.description:
A plane to start from, kept as a plane so the bodies follow it when it moves; the bodies
turn so that it meets the target. Not with `from`, `from_face` or `from_frame`.

name.description: The feature's name in the timeline.

participants.description:
The bodies taking part, each an existing body or `*`; what that changes depends on the
feature.

to.description:
Where the bodies go. Not read when `to_face` is a point; not with `to_plane` or
`to_frame`.

to_face.description:
A point on a planar face to go to. When it is a point, `to` is not read. Not with
`to_plane` or `to_frame`.

to_frame.description:
A frame to go to, in place of the point, face or plane. It must not be on a body that
moves. Not with `to`, `to_face` or `to_plane`.

to_plane.description:
A plane to go to, which may move later (the bodies follow); a point or a face goes onto
it along its normal. Not with `to`, `to_face` or `to_frame`.

type?: constant|curvature (alias g2: curvature-continuous quintic between planar faces along straight edges, one planar end face at each end (including sloped ends); radius sets the equivalent circular setback, not constant curvature; exact fit only)|chord (radius is the width across)|variable (radius at the end nearest start, radius2 at the other; one end may be 0, where the round closes to the corner)|spline (the radius along the edge is a clamped B-spline from the end nearest start: radius is its first control radius, radii the rest, knots its knot vector from 0 to 1; one end may be 0); radius2?; start?: [x,y,z]; radii?: [expr, …]; knots?: [number, …]; mid?: [[position 0…1 from start, radius expr], …] (variable radii between the ends); smooth?: bool (smooth instead of straight between the radii); corner?: rolling|g2 (rolling, the default: the corners where three blended edges meet are pieces of the rolling ball's sphere, tangent to each blend; a curvature round's corners are always g2 patches, between its own sections; g2: each corner where three or more rounded edges meet, and every edge there is rounded, is set back (1.5 × the radius along each edge unless `setbacks` names it) and filled with a patch meeting the rounds and the faces round it to the second order (curvature-continuous seams, clear of the points where a round's section ends on a face), constant-radius exact fillets only, refused where it cannot be built); setbacks?: [{vertex: [x,y,z], distance: expr}, …] (corner setbacks: the corner at the vertex nearest `vertex`, where every edge meeting it is rounded, starts its patch `distance` along each of those edges from the vertex, past where the rounds would meet (past the radius at a square corner), so the rounds blend through a larger patch; one distance for all of a corner's edges; constant-radius exact fillets only; with `corner: g2`, the G2 patch's corners); turn?: mitre|swept (where two rounds turn round a sharp, straight, convex side edge square to both on a plane, such as the rounds along a boss's base at its upright edges: mitre, the default, runs them on to meet in a mitre; swept ends them at the side edge and fills the corner with their section revolved about it, a torus; swept takes type: constant, corner: rolling, no setbacks and fit: exact or reduce, and is refused with the reason where the rounds are unequal or the side edge is concave, curved or tangent); fit?: exact|reduce|taper (exact, the default: a radius too large for the geometry around the edges is refused, naming the largest that fits; reduce: where it doesn't fit it is reduced to the largest that does, one radius for edges sharing a face; the smallest used is returned as `radius_applied`, each edge's as `radii_applied: [{edge: [x,y,z], radius}]`, and noted in the feature's warning; taper: along each straight edge between planar faces where it doesn't fit, the radius follows the room there as a smooth spline, down to 0 where a face closes to a point, noted in the feature's warning)

convention.description: Where the angle starts. Default: sketch_normal.

points. The handler ignores every other value.

profile that reference geometry (a face's projected outline) cuts into regions takes the

and `direction`.

input.description:
`view.navigate`: turn, pan, orbit or zoom a camera without changing the design or adding to
undo. `camera` is always needed, and then one of three: `direction` (look from it), `action`
(a turn, a roll, home or fit) or `motion` (direct manipulation, which wins when given and
does not take `fit`). Keys of the other forms are not used.

action.description:
A turn without `direction`: left, right, up or down turn the view `degrees`, clockwise and
counterclockwise roll it a quarter turn, home shows the isometric view framed, fit frames
the model.

anchor.description: Zoom towards this point (mm). Default: the camera's target.

camera.description:
The camera to move, as `ui.inspect` gives it. Its yaw and roll must also be within ±1e6
and its pitch within ±π/2.

degrees.description: How far left, right, up or down turn the view, above 0 and at most 180. Default: 90.

delta.description: Pan or orbit by this many pixels.

direction.description:
Look from this direction, in the camera's up-axis frame: a finite nonzero vector of
length at most 2.

fit.description:
Also frame the whole model from the new direction, as home does. Not with `motion`.
Default: false.

free_orbit.description: Orbit through the poles. Default: false.

motion.description:
Direct manipulation: pan and orbit need `delta`, pan and an orbit about a `pivot` need
`viewport`, zoom needs `factor`.

pivot.description: Orbit about this point (mm) rather than the camera's target.

viewport.description: The viewport's size in pixels, for a pan or an orbit about a pivot.
